title: Stranded in Germany on a one-way ticket
summary: A film producer sent him a one-way ticket to Germany with no contract signed; the American Consulate makes Lee Bouveau pay for lodging.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, we're going to jump around a little bit now. We just want to fill in a few holes, okay? We'll do this from time to time. We're with you when you're in Germany now. You're there stranded. You received a ticket from the producers of this film that you were supposed to be in to come to Germany.
It was a one-way ticket. You got there, you realized that there was no contract signed, the deal was off.

I don't get to realize nothing. Take it the way it goes. The film company wanted to get a signature from the agent that told them about me and they paid the one-way ticket to be sure I would be there. Send me a round-trip ticket? No, that was too much to do. They send me a one-way ticket, it's easy

to get the ticket going back if I'm going to work for them. But they sent the one-way ticket. I don't know. They tell me they're going to give me a thousand dollars a week and all expenses paid, so I'm beginning to wonder - I don't got but the one-way ticket, 'cause I had to pay my own fare out of the thousand dollars. I'm not worried about not paying me. I'm just worried about getting over there, that's all. But I didn't know there wasn't going to be no job. That's the way it was. I didn't know there wasn't going to be no job for me. When I found out there wasn't going to be no job, then that's when I had to go to the American Consulate to get advice as to what my next move should be and the American Consulate took it over. He said to Lee Bouveau that "you've got to pay for that hotel he's in and you've got to pay for his living while he's here. So Lee Bouveau got another place for me to live that he had to pay for. He had to pay for it but I don't think he paid for it, I think the
agency paid for it because they okayed me to leave there to go to Kaiserslautern.
